text: A thousand metres down, it's always night. So how does anything live here?
Some life clings to underwater volcanoes. These shrimp crowd around vents spitting water over four hundred degrees.
Almost three thousand metres. The deepest dive by any mammal, Cuvier's beaked whale. One held its breath for over three hours.
At three thousand eight hundred lies the Titanic. The pressure is three hundred and eighty times the surface. Yet fangtooth fish, hagfish and dumbo octopuses live here.
At eight thousand three hundred: the deepest fish ever filmed. A little snailfish.
Remember Everest? Flip it over, and its peak stops here. Still not the bottom.
The bottom is almost eleven kilometres down. Two men first reached it in 1960. The next was James Cameron, fifty-two years later.
We've been to the bottom. But most of the deep sea, no one has ever seen.
So next time you're at the beach, don't look too far down. Something might be looking back.
